scope: 2025-2026 conference editions; selected 2025 model report. Not an exhaustive awards list or citation ranking.
rights: Original PDFs and rendered excerpts remain local reference materials. Repository ships metadata and code only. Verify asset-specific reuse terms before redistribution.

entries.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
entries.observed: A large scene reconstruction occupies the center, with a narrow stack of input views and smaller tracking/depth evidence around it.
entries.adaptation: Let one actual scene dominate. Keep matching camera/view evidence small but legible; connect only corresponding regions.
entries.avoid: Do not enlarge a decorative scene while hiding the actual reconstruction or reuse invented depth maps.

entries.title: Efficiently Reconstructing Dynamic Scenes One D4RT at a Time
entries.observed: Rows align the same dynamic input with reconstruction outputs from several methods; geometry and trajectories coexist in the comparison.
entries.adaptation: Compare motion-aware scene reconstructions under the same input and preserve each method label and trajectory legend.
entries.avoid: Do not interpret trajectory colors as segmentation classes or describe a static reconstruction as a generated video.

entries.title: Native and Compact Structured Latents for 3D Generation
entries.observed: Large reconstruction and generation specimens combine normals, material breakdowns and smaller views; compact quantitative plots sit at the side.
entries.adaptation: Place a detailed asset beside genuinely corresponding geometry/material passes. Add a small efficiency chart only when measured data are available.
entries.avoid: Do not fabricate material channels, normals, token counts or efficiency measurements to complete the composition.

entries.title: Generating Physically Stable and Buildable Brick Structures from Text
entries.observed: Intermediate construction views share a band with human/robot assembly photos; a separate gallery demonstrates output diversity.
entries.adaptation: Pair a digital result with the actual fabricated object or real execution, and use short chronological assembly samples.
entries.avoid: The transferable idea is physical verification, not a requirement to turn unrelated tasks into brick scenes.

entries.title: FEAST: A Flexible Mealtime-Assistance System Towards In-the-Wild Personalization
entries.observed: A compact study/design rationale sits beside a larger mosaic of people using the robot across real home contexts.
entries.adaptation: For human-centered deployment, show actual usage contexts and framing variation rather than only robot hardware close-ups.
entries.avoid: Do not infer user outcomes from a photo; retain participant consent, privacy treatment and source-specific reuse terms.

entries.title: Fabrica: Dual-Arm Assembly of General Multi-Part Objects via Integrated Planning and Learning
entries.observed: Three task rows show successive real dual-arm interactions for different objects on a consistent work surface.
entries.adaptation: Use one row per task; sample contact and assembly transitions rather than repeating nearly identical idle frames.
entries.avoid: Shown samples are not necessarily contiguous frames or equal time intervals; do not label every endpoint a success.

entries.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
entries.observed: Two aligned rows show the same dog sequence before and after an additional interaction; the prompt frame and correction are explicitly marked.
entries.adaptation: Use synchronized before/after frame positions for interactive corrections; preserve object identity and overlay-color meaning.
entries.avoid: Do not call this Best Paper, or repaint masks with arbitrary aesthetic colors that change object correspondence.

entries.title: CAST: Component-Aligned 3D Scene Reconstruction from an RGB Image
entries.observed: An interlocking gallery presents many reconstructed scenes with a consistent elevated viewpoint and visually varied contents.
entries.adaptation: Unify lighting and camera convention while varying the actual scenes; use a gallery when diversity itself is evidenced.
entries.avoid: Do not copy the tessellated layout so densely that object occlusion hides reconstruction errors.

entries.title: TokenVerse: Versatile Multi-concept Personalization in Token Modulation Space
entries.observed: A narrow concept-image rail feeds three larger composed outputs; corresponding words and source concepts share selective color cues.
entries.adaptation: Use small real reference images above large compositional results, linking only the concepts actually conditioned on.
entries.avoid: Do not represent an output as a conditioning image, or imply a concept transfer that the shown run did not perform.

entries.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
entries.observed: Baseline and gated-model rows align a layer-wise summary curve with matching attention maps.
entries.adaptation: For mechanism evidence, align quantitative summaries with raw matrix evidence, retaining axes, scales and experimental conditions.
entries.avoid: This is a chart reference, not a photo-teaser preset. Never replace actual attention data with decorative heatmaps.

entries.title: Score Matching with Missing Data
entries.observed: A compact method comparison uses labeled axes, a legend and visible uncertainty intervals across sample sizes.
entries.adaptation: Retain statistical definitions and readable intervals when inserting a small quantitative panel beside qualitative results.
entries.avoid: Do not infer uncertainty from line thickness or copy a caption without checking the plotted axis and metric.

entries.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
entries.observed: Rows of six ordered outputs cover varied subjects and aspect ratios; the page is dominated by generated frames rather than a method diagram.
entries.adaptation: Use multiple subjects and meaningful motion samples; keep within-sequence framing consistent and place prompt details in the caption.
entries.avoid: Representative model selection is not an award or a citation ranking. Do not equate six shown samples with a six-frame generated clip.
